question: persister
prompt:
Each of your ideas must draw on a domain unrelated to the research question below, for example through an analogy, a structure, a principle, or a pattern borrowed from that domain, while still being a concrete, scientifically sound way to address the question.

Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Reliability-engineering hazard analysis of single-cell death times
ideas.description: Borrowing from reliability engineering, track individual cells by live imaging under constant drug and fit Weibull or other hazard models to their time-to-death. A shape parameter near 1 suggests random, state-independent survival, while a shape far from 1 points to survival governed by cell age, cycle phase, or an accumulating state.

ideas.title: Wafer-map spatial yield analysis of surviving colonies
ideas.description: Borrowing from semiconductor yield analysis, map every surviving cell or colony's position on the culture and apply point-pattern and spatial autocorrelation statistics (e.g., Ripley's K, Moran's I). Clustering would implicate local microenvironment such as density, oxygen, or drug gradients, whereas a random scatter would support intrinsic stochastic survival.

ideas.title: Phylodynamic reconstruction of persister ancestry
ideas.description: Borrowing from epidemiological phylodynamics, combine CRISPR lineage barcodes with single-cell transcriptomes to reconstruct the transmission-like tree of surviving cells. Few early founder clades with pre-existing transcriptional states would suggest pre-selection, while many independent lineages that converge on a shared state after treatment would suggest adaptive induction.

ideas.title: Mutual-information budget between pre-treatment states and survival
ideas.description: Borrowing from information theory, sort live cells by pre-treatment reporter or transcriptional state and quantify the mutual information between that state and eventual survival after drug exposure. Near-zero information would indicate survival is essentially random, while significant information would identify which features are predictive and how much of the outcome they explain.

ideas.title: Pulsed-dosing system identification of feedback in survivor cells
ideas.description: Borrowing from control engineering, apply pulsed or step drug inputs of varying amplitude and duration while recording live signaling reporters, then estimate an input-output transfer function for each cell. Ringing, delayed responses, or bistable switching in the fitted model would expose the feedback loops or memory elements that let a subpopulation stay in a tolerant state.
